q: מטופל עם דמנציה מתקדמת מאושפז במחלקה הפנימית עם אבחנה של דלקת ראות. נקראת לתת ייעוץ לקביעת מטרות טיפוליות. לפי המאמר Advanced dementia של Mitchell מה משמעות הטיפול האנטיביוטי בחולה במצב זה?
o: על פי מחקרים אקראיים כפולי סמיות, טיפול אנטיביוטי הוא בעל ערך בהורדת נטל סימפטומים בחולים אלו
טיפול אנטיביוטי בדלקת ריאות יעיל בהארכת חיים במטופלים אלו, אולם גם הגביר את הסבל מסימפטומים גופניים
טיפול אנטיביוטי הוכח כמקל על סימפטומים רק בזיהומים בדרכי השתן
מחלה זיהומית היא הסיבה השכיחה ביותר לסימפטומים גופניים בחולי דמנציה סופנית ולכן יש לתת טיפול אנטיביוטי אצלם מוקדם ככל האפשר
explanation:
Distinguish **longer survival** from **comfort**. The evidence described in the book does not show that both improve together, so treatment should reflect the goals of care (p. 1048).

**A. Double-blind randomized trials show that antibiotics reduce symptom burden.** Wrong, the described evidence is observational, not double-blind randomized proof of symptom relief. Longer survival does not establish improved comfort (p. 1048).
**B. Antibiotics for pneumonia prolong life but increase physical discomfort.** Correct, this is the official choice: antibiotics were associated with longer survival without improved comfort, and more aggressive treatment was associated with greater discomfort (p. 1048).
**C. Antibiotics have proven symptom-relieving benefit only in urinary tract infections.** Wrong, this page does not establish exclusive proven symptom relief in urinary infections; it emphasizes the patient's goals rather than guaranteed symptomatic benefit from treating a particular infection (p. 1048).
**D. Infection is the most common cause of physical symptoms in terminal dementia, so antibiotics should always be given as early as possible.** Wrong, frequent infection does not mandate early antibiotics in every situation. Treatment depends on the patient's goals and avoidance of unwanted burden (p. 1048).

Supplementary-source support: Antibiotics for aspiration pneumonia in advanced dementia were associated with longer survival but not improved comfort. Intravenous therapy and hospitalization were associated with the greatest discomfort, whereas survival benefit was similar across administration routes. This supports the officially accepted statement while distinguishing survival from comfort (Hazzard 8e, p. 1048).

Supplementary source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1048. The original Mitchell article reference remains in the official bibliography field.

q: What defines palliative sedation in Hazzard?
o: Reduce consciousness intentionally to relieve refractory end-of-life suffering
Medication administration intended to bring about the patient’s death
Withdrawal of life-prolonging treatment without intentionally reducing consciousness
Routine analgesia preserving consciousness without an intended sedative intervention
explanation:
**Palliative sedation** intentionally lowers consciousness to relieve intractable symptoms at the end of life. Hazzard describes it as “intentionally lowering the patient’s level of consciousness using sedating medications” (p. 1105). It is an intervention of last resort within interdisciplinary palliative care, and its use should not be expected to shorten time to death (p. 1105).

**A. Reduce consciousness intentionally to relieve refractory end-of-life suffering.** Correct, it includes the intended reduction of consciousness and refractory-symptom relief that define the intervention (p. 1105).
**B. Medication administration intended to bring about the patient’s death.** Wrong, the source specifies use where it is not expected to shorten time to death; causing death is not its therapeutic intent (p. 1105).
**C. Withdrawal of life-prolonging treatment without intentionally reducing consciousness.** Wrong, withdrawal without a sedative reduction in consciousness does not meet the defining intervention described here (p. 1105).
**D. Routine analgesia preserving consciousness without an intended sedative intervention.** Wrong, analgesia that preserves consciousness is distinct from the intentional reduction of consciousness defining palliative sedation (p. 1105).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1105.

q: אישה בת 84 עם דמנציה קלה (MMSE 22) המתגוררת בבית עם בתה מובאת לחדר מיון לאחר fall. היא נוטלת donepezil 10 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, ו-aspirin 81 mg ביום. בתה מדווחת על קושי הולך וגובר בניהול כספים ותרופות במשך 3 חודשים, וכעת דורשת השגחה על כל ה-IADLs. בבדיקה גופנית: חבורות באזור הירך, סימנים חיוניים תקינים, ללא ממצאים נוירולוגיים פוקאליים. X-ray ירך תקין. Creatinine clearance הוא 42 mL/min. איזו התערבות תפחית ביעילות הרבה ביותר את הסיכון ל-falls עתידיים ולירידה תפקודית?
o: הפניה למוסד שיקומי אשפוזי
הרשמה לתכנית PACE
התחלת memantine 5 mg ביום
מרשם ל-hip protectors ו-vitamin D
explanation:
התשובה הנכונה היא הרשמה לתכנית PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly). מטופלת זו מדגימה ירידה תפקודית הפוגעת ב-IADLs, עברה fall, ועומדת בקריטריונים לקבלה ל-PACE: גיל ≥55, הוגדרה כזקוקה לרמת טיפול של בית אבות, ומסוגלת לחיות בבטחה בקהילה עם שירותי תמיכה. PACE מספקת טיפול מקיף ורב-מקצועי הכולל PT/OT, ניהול תרופתי, שירותים סוציאליים ותכניות יום — המתייחסת לכלל גורמי הסיכון שלה.

אפשרות A (שיקום אשפוזי) היא תשובת המלכודת — רבים מהרופאים שולחים באופן רפלקטיבי קשישים שנפלו לשיקום. אולם, אין לה פציעה חריפה המצריכה טיפול אינטנסיבי, והיא תרוויח יותר מטיפול מקיף בקהילה.

אפשרות C (memantine) עשויה לסייע במידה מסוימת ל-cognition, אך לא תטפל בסיכון ל-falls, בירידה ב-IADLs, או בבעיות ניהול התרופות. עם CrCl של 42 mL/min, יידרש התאמת מינון.

אפשרות D (hip protectors/vitamin D) אינה מספקת — מתייחסת להגנה מכנית בלבד, ולא לגורמים המולטיפקטוריאליים של הירידה שלה.

Pearl קליני: תכניות PACE מפחיתות אשפוזים ב-30% וקבלה לבתי אבות ב-50% באמצעות טיפול רב-מקצועי פרואקטיבי. הן אידיאליות לקשישים עם frailty וירידה תפקודית שעדיין יכולים לחיות בבית עם תמיכה.

q: An 85-year-old man becomes confused on the second day after total knee arthroplasty. He pulls at his urinary catheter and fails to recognize his family. He has treated hypertension, normal serum chemistry and recent opioid exposure for postoperative pain. No focal neurologic signs or head trauma are found, and the catheter no longer has a clinical indication. Which action fits initial nonpharmacologic delirium management?
o: Start scheduled haloperidol before environmental measures
Remove the unnecessary urinary catheter
Obtain routine head CT before addressing contributors
Add clonidine specifically to treat the delirium
explanation:
**Nonpharmacologic strategies** begin delirium management and include minimizing immobilizing equipment such as bladder catheters. Evaluation of causes and medication exposure continues alongside these measures; an unnecessary catheter is a modifiable factor in this stem (pp. 885, 888).
"Minimizing immobilizing equipment (eg, restraints, bladder catheters)" (p. 888).
"The recommended management approach for all delirious patients begins with nonpharmacologic strategies" (p. 888).

**A. Start scheduled haloperidol before environmental measures.** Wrong, antipsychotics are a last resort for selected cases, rather than a substitute for initial nonpharmacologic measures (pp. 888-889).
**B. Remove the unnecessary urinary catheter.** Correct, removing the unnecessary catheter follows the recommendation to minimize immobilizing equipment (p. 888).
**C. Obtain routine head CT before addressing contributors.** Wrong, routine imaging is not the first response in the absence of focal signs, trauma or an unexplained syndrome; clinical evaluation and addressing contributors remain central (p. 885).
**D. Add clonidine specifically to treat the delirium.** Wrong, the source reports no detected effect of clonidine on delirium (p. 889).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 885, 888, 889.

q: A woman after a stroke can transfer to a commode, but cognitive impairment prevents her from requesting help in time. There are no signs of infection or urinary retention. Staff are available to help. Which intervention is appropriate?
o: Emphasize independently performed pelvic floor muscle exercises
Emphasize a bladder diary maintained by the patient herself
Provide assisted toileting at regularly scheduled intervals
Emphasize independently lengthening the intervals between voids
explanation:
**Scheduled toileting** is a caregiver-dependent intervention that does not rely on the patient initiating a request. Hazzard defines it as "Routine toileting at regular intervals" and allows its use with impaired cognition when a caregiver is available (p. 710). Patient-dependent approaches require the ability to learn and practice (p. 709).

**A. Emphasize independently performed pelvic floor muscle exercises.** Wrong, independent pelvic floor training requires functional ability and motivation; it does not supply the caregiver assistance needed for her failure to initiate toileting (pp. 709–710).
**B. Emphasize a bladder diary maintained by the patient herself.** Wrong, a self-maintained diary is part of patient-dependent training, whereas her stated difficulty calls for caregiver-dependent toileting (pp. 709–710).
**C. Provide assisted toileting at regularly scheduled intervals.** Correct, this matches scheduled toileting and the available staff support in a patient with impaired cognition (p. 710).
**D. Emphasize independently lengthening the intervals between voids.** Wrong, independent bladder retraining requires adequate cognitive function and motivation, whereas scheduled assistance addresses the stated limitation (p. 710).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 710, 709.

q: בן 86, הגיע למרפאה עקב תלונות על גרד ואודם ברגליים, שידוע מזה זמן רב, אך. לאחרונה החמיר. בבדיקתו רושם לעור מחוספס ומגרד, יבש, סדוק תמונה מספר 2 מה הטיפול הראשוני לממצאים בעור?
o: אנטיביוטיקה מקומית ( Benzoil peroxide, Erythromycin ו- metronidazole)
חומרי לחות, קורטיקוסטרואידים מקומיים קלים לזמן מוגבל
נוגדי פטריות מקומיים (Miconazole)
Crotamiton ( סקביצין)
explanation:
Dry, rough, cracked, inflamed skin on the shins fits **asteatotic eczema**. Water loss through a damaged skin barrier explains the dryness; treatment restores moisture and reduces inflammation (DermNet, Causes; Treatment).

**A. Topical antibiotics.** Wrong, by clinical inference, the described problem is dryness and dermatitis rather than bacterial infection; antibiotics do not address the principal process described (DermNet, Causes; Treatment).
**B. Moisturisers and mild topical corticosteroids for a limited period.** Correct, emollients address dryness and a brief course of mild topical steroid treats reddened, inflamed skin (DermNet, Treatment).
**C. Topical antifungals.** Wrong, the stem gives no finding pointing to fungal infection. By inference, treatment should address dryness and inflammation (DermNet, Clinical features; Treatment).
**D. Crotamiton.** Wrong as the proposed initial treatment here; by inference, treating itch alone is not equivalent to the combined moisture-restoring and anti-inflammatory approach described (DermNet, Treatment).

Source: Oakley A. Asteatotic eczema. DermNet, updated July 2014, Causes, Clinical features, Treatment. https://dermnetnz.org/topics/asteatotic-eczema.

q: בת 75, מתגוררת בדיור מוגן, מתניידת עם הליכון, לוקה בדמנציה, תחת טיפול ב- MEMANTINE. מתקבלת לאשפוז במחלקה פנימית בשל דלקת ריאות ומקבלת טיפול אנטיביוטי ב- CEFTRIAXONE וטיפול מניעתי ב- OMEPRAZOL ו- ENOXAPARIN. לשינה טופלה ב- ZOLPIDEM. ביום השני לאשפוזה החולה מבולבלת, באי שקט ניכר וצועקת. בשיחה איתה, נראה כי היא חושבת שהיא נמצאת כעת בביתה. איזה טיפול תרופתי יכול לגרום למצבה בסבירות הגבוהה ביותר?
o: ZOLPIDEM
OMEPRAZOLE
MEMANTINE
CEFTRIAXONE
explanation:
Acute disorientation and behavioral change on a background of dementia fit **delirium**. Dementia increases vulnerability to acute triggers including illness and medications. **Zolpidem** is explicitly listed among drugs that can precipitate or worsen delirium, making it a clear target when reviewing newly added treatment (Hazzard 8e, pp. 882-883; Beers 2023, p. 2060).

**A. Zolpidem.** Correct, this newly added hypnotic is explicitly associated with delirium. Inference for the case: new exposure plus dementia supports the official choice without attributing every episode to the drug alone (Hazzard, p. 883; Beers, p. 2060).
**B. Omeprazole.** Wrong, it is not the sedating drug highlighted in the table and must not be confused with the H2 blockers that are listed. Absence from the table does not prove zero risk, but does not provide the direct support present for zolpidem (Hazzard, p. 883).
**C. Memantine.** Wrong, confusion is a listed adverse effect, but this is prior treatment rather than the newly added sleep drug. That is a temporal inference from the stem, not a claim that memantine cannot contribute (Hazzard, p. 913).
**D. Ceftriaxone.** Wrong, under the official key. Nevertheless, encephalopathy and confusion have been reported, particularly with older age and renal impairment. Routine dosing does not establish negligible risk, and the article gives no direct probability comparison with zolpidem for this case (Lacroix et al., sections 2.4, 3).

Antibiotic and anticoagulant use alone is not presented as an automatic indication for omeprazole on the cited page (Hazzard, p. 883).
Memantine is absent from Table 58-2, but confusion appears in its adverse-effect profile in Table 59-7; zolpidem remains the officially preferred explanation among the choices here (Hazzard, pp. 883, 913).
Sedating and psychoactive drugs are associated with delirium; the cited pages do not provide a zolpidem-specific first-night estimate (Hazzard, pp. 882-883).
Note: Choosing zolpidem does not exclude additional causes of delirium, and the case does not prove single-drug causation.
Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 882-883, 913; AGS Beers 2023, p. 2060; Lacroix C et al. Serious Neurological Adverse Events of Ceftriaxone. Antibiotics. 2021;10:540, sections 2.4, 3, doi:10.3390/antibiotics10050540.

q: איזה מהשינויים הבאים מתרחש באופן פיזיולוגי בתפקודי התריס בגיל המבוגר?
o: ישנם פחות נוגדנים עצמיים
TBG (Thyroid-binding globulin) עולה
רמות T4 יורדות
TSH עולה
explanation:
**TSH** rises slightly with normal aging. This alone does not indicate occult thyroid failure: free T4 remains stable, and changes in TSH bioactivity or thyroid sensitivity may contribute (Hazzard 8e, p. 1546).

**A. Fewer thyroid autoantibodies.** Wrong, thyroid autoantibody prevalence increases in older adults, particularly women, consistent with more autoimmune thyroid disease (p. 1546).
**B. Increased thyroid-binding globulin.** Wrong, TBG concentration remains unchanged with aging rather than increasing physiologically (p. 1546).
**C. Reduced T4 levels.** Wrong, secretion and clearance decline together, maintaining stable hormone concentrations. Reduced production does not imply lower circulating T4 (p. 1546).
**D. Increased TSH.** Correct, TSH gradually rises even without thyroid disease or autoimmunity and without a decline in free T4 (p. 1546).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1546.

q: Which SSRI should be avoided in older adults because of anticholinergic activity and delirium risk?
o: Escitalopram
Paroxetine
Citalopram
Sertraline
explanation:
Paroxetine has anticholinergic activity and increased delirium risk; the text advises avoiding it in older adults (p929–930).

C. Citalopram: Its highlighted distinguishing concern is QTc prolongation, not the paroxetine anticholinergic warning (p929).
A. Escitalopram: Table 60-9 lists GI effects, hyponatremia, insomnia and fatigue; the anticholinergic avoidance warning names paroxetine (p929–930).
D. Sertraline: Its listed effects include GI effects, hyponatremia and headache; the anticholinergic warning names paroxetine (p929–930).

q: Why does adequate control of acute postoperative pain matter for an older adult’s longer-term recovery?
o: Poorly controlled pain may protect against chronic pain by reducing mobility demands.
Poorly controlled pain may shorten admission by limiting excessive postoperative activity.
Appropriate pain control may help prevent chronic pain and pain-related mobility limitations.
Appropriate pain control may improve comfort while increasing the later risk of chronic pain.
explanation:
**Acute pain control** matters beyond immediate comfort, because poorly controlled postoperative pain is associated with limited mobility and prolonged admission (p. 1055). The chapter adds that “acute pain that is appropriately managed during the perioperative period may help prevent the development of chronic pain.” (p. 1055).

**A. Poorly controlled pain may protect against chronic pain by reducing mobility demands.** Wrong, poor control is associated with limited mobility and increased chronic-pain risk; pain-related immobility is not described as protective (p. 1055).
**B. Poorly controlled pain may shorten admission by limiting excessive postoperative activity.** Wrong, poor control is associated with prolonged hospital stays, contradicting the proposed shorter admission (p. 1055).
**C. Appropriate pain control may help prevent chronic pain and pain-related mobility limitations.** Correct, the page reports adverse mobility consequences of poor control and possible prevention of chronic pain with appropriate perioperative management (p. 1055).
**D. Appropriate pain control may improve comfort while increasing the later risk of chronic pain.** Wrong, the stated later effect is possible prevention of chronic pain, rather than increased chronic-pain risk (p. 1055).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1055.

q: Why can a rising serum creatinine be pathological even when it remains near the laboratory normal range?
o: A value at the upper limit of normal excludes significant loss of renal function
Serum creatinine should rise with normal aging and need not affect renal drug dosing
Creatinine production increases as muscle mass falls, so a rising level is normal aging
Muscle loss reduces creatinine production, so serum creatinine should remain relatively constant
explanation:
Loss of muscle mass reduces creatinine production, so serum creatinine should remain relatively constant and an upper-normal level can reflect important renal decline (p1268).

C. Creatinine production increases as muscle mass falls, so a rising level is normal aging: The book describes reduced creatinine production with loss of muscle mass (p1268).
A. A value at the upper limit of normal excludes significant loss of renal function: The book states that an upper-normal level can represent significant decline in an older individual (p1268).
B. Serum creatinine should rise with normal aging and need not affect renal drug dosing: The book says creatinine should remain relatively constant and elevations warrant attention to renal function and dosing (p1268).
